title: Weather Delays a Cargo Capsule's Return From the International Space Station! 🌊
body: Weather Delays a Cargo Capsule's Return From the International Space Station! 🌊

The undocking of SpaceX's Dragon cargo capsule from the International Space Station was delayed on Wednesday due to bad weather at the landing sites off the coast of California. The capsule is returning science and supplies, including samples of 3D-printed blood vessels and frozen tumor samples for research on Earth. The next undocking opportunity was Thursday afternoon, and no new return date has been set yet.

The capsule lands by parachute in the Pacific Ocean, so the wind and waves must be calm — like waiting for good weather before a boat trip. The delay is a routine safety measure, not a malfunction: the capsule and the station are fine. This is SpaceX's 35th commercial resupply mission.
Did you think weather could affect even a spacecraft's return from space? 🌤️
